data.name: Step1_Description
data.value:
For Windows x64, download the latest standalone executable: [Download yt-dlp.exe (latest release)]({0})
For full YouTube support, also download and extract Deno: [Download Deno for Windows x64 (ZIP, latest release)]({1})
Keep yt-dlp.exe and the extracted deno.exe in a permanent local folder. The official standalone yt-dlp release includes the EJS scripts; Python is not required.
Other platforms and release details: [yt-dlp releases]({2}) · [Deno releases]({3})

data.name: Step2_Headline
data.value: Select binaries and link FFmpeg tools

data.name: Step2_Description
data.value:
Configure this provider:
- **yt-dlp executable** → e.g. C:\Tools\Media\yt-dlp.exe - **Deno executable** → e.g. C:\Tools\Media\deno.exe - **Shared FFmpeg tools** → create or link an **FFmpeg tools** object.
Open the FFmpeg tools object's **Quick Start**. That guide provides its download link and explains the binary directory. Reuse an existing tools object when FFmpeg is already installed. Configure the FFmpeg binary directory on that tools object.
The tools must be available on the computer executing the flow, including CLI/service runs.

data.name: Step3_Description
data.value:
Save this provider and select it in the **Media download** FlowBlock.
Use a video URL supported by yt-dlp, such as a YouTube video page. A playlist URL selects its first item. Iterate separate video URLs in the flow for multiple downloads. Adjust this provider's timeout for long downloads and conversion.
The FlowBlock's own **Quick Start** explains source fields, output directory, output format and result fields. Reopen this provider's guide at any time using its **Quick Start** action.
